title: Design a Scalable Multi-Channel Notification Engine
summary: Design an enterprise-scale distributed notification engine supporting prioritized email, SMS, push notifications, and in-app alerts with user preferences and deduplication.
description: Design a distributed notification system powering customer communications across iOS Push (APNs), Android Push (FCM), SMS (Twilio), and transactional Email (SendGrid/SES). The platform ingests notification triggers from upstream microservices, enforces user channel preferences and quiet-hour windows, deduplicates repetitive events, dynamically throttles dispatch to adhere to third-party vendor rate limits, and provides comprehensive delivery tracking with dead-letter queue resilience.
functional_requirements: Support multiple delivery channels: Mobile Push (APNs, FCM), SMS, Transactional Email, and In-App notification feed.
Enforce user preferences and opt-out rules per category (security, transactional, marketing), including time-zone aware quiet hours.
Classify notifications into priority tiers: High Priority (OTPs, fraud alerts) and Low/Bulk Priority (newsletters, promotional offers).
Perform automated deduplication within a configurable sliding time window (e.g. 10 minutes) using idempotency keys.
Support localized dynamic template rendering with parameter interpolation.
Track end-to-end delivery lifecycle states (queued, dispatched, delivered, bounced, opened, failed) and expose status query APIs.
non_functional_requirements: High Throughput: Ingest and process 100,000,000 notifications per day with peak burst handling of 10,000 QPS.
Guaranteed At-Least-Once Delivery: Critical security notifications must never be dropped due to system crashes or temporary node restarts.
Low Latency for High-Priority Alerts: High-priority security messages must reach third-party gateways within 5 seconds (p99).
Third-Party Provider Fault Tolerance: Resilient circuit breaking with automatic multi-vendor failover (e.g. fallback from primary SMS provider to backup).
Strict Isolation: Bulk promotional campaigns must never block or degrade transactional verification message throughput.
key_challenges: Idempotency & Deduplication: Constructing deterministic cache keys in Redis (SHA256 of user_id + event_type + content_hash) with atomic SETNX to prevent duplicate user annoyance.
Priority inversion prevention: Isolating high-priority transactional traffic from massive bulk marketing campaigns using dedicated partitioned queue topics.
Third-party rate limiting & backpressure: Implementing distributed Token Bucket limiters per external provider to avoid HTTP 429 throttling and account suspension.
Stale device token cleanup: Processing feedback loops from Apple APNs and Google FCM to deactivate invalid registration tokens.
Resilience with Dead Letter Queues (DLQ): Moving permanently failed notifications to a DLQ after exponential backoff retries for manual audit or batch reprocessing.

reference_solution.architecture_pattern: Asynchronous event-driven pipeline utilizing distributed message brokers, decoupled worker pools, and priority queues
core_components: Stateless Notification Ingestion Gateway exposing REST/gRPC endpoints and validating idempotency keys
Redis Cluster storing active idempotency keys with TTL and caching user delivery preference profiles
Apache Kafka message broker maintaining segregated topics (priority.high, priority.medium, priority.bulk)
Template Rendering Engine fetching localized templates and interpolating dynamic variables
Channel Dispatcher Workers (Push Workers, SMS Workers, Email Workers) managing outbound connection pools
Provider Adapter Layer with client-side rate limiting and automatic multi-vendor circuit breaker failover
Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) capturing unrecoverable delivery failures after 5 exponential backoff retries
Delivery Status Webhook Receiver updating notification status records in PostgreSQL and ClickHouse
reference_solution.deduplication_strategy: Redis SET key value NX EX 600 using a deterministic hash of (user_id, category, idempotency_token). If the key exists, the request returns 200 OK immediately without queuing duplicate messages.
reference_solution.priority_routing: High-priority messages bypass standard queues and route to a dedicated Kafka topic with over-provisioned worker pools, guaranteeing sub-5 second delivery.
